name: global
description: Region-independent red flags that appear in scam messages worldwide.

rules.title: Pressure to act quickly
rules.explanation: Scammers rush you so you do not stop to think or check. Real organisations rarely demand action within hours.

rules.title: Threatens your account or service
rules.explanation: Messages that say your account will be locked, suspended or closed unless you click are a classic phishing hook.

rules.title: Asks you to share a code, PIN or password
rules.explanation: No genuine bank, wallet or service will ask you to send or read out a one-time code, PIN, password or card security code.

rules.title: Claims you have won something
rules.explanation: Unexpected prizes, lotteries and rewards you never entered are used to lure you into paying a fee or giving details.

rules.title: Asks for payment in a hard-to-trace way
rules.explanation: Gift cards, crypto and wire transfers are favoured by scammers because they are hard to reverse or trace.

rules.title: Delivery problem with a fee or address request
rules.explanation: Fake courier messages ask for a small 'redelivery' or customs fee, or for your address and card details.

rules.title: Threatens arrest, fines or legal action
rules.explanation: Fear of arrest or prosecution is used to force quick payment. Authorities do not demand payment by text message.

rules.title: Promises easy or guaranteed money
rules.explanation: Guaranteed returns, doubled money and high pay for simple remote tasks are hallmarks of investment and job scams.

rules.title: Asks you to keep it secret
rules.explanation: Scammers isolate victims so friends and family cannot spot the scam.

rules.title: 'Hi Mum/Dad, this is my new number' pattern
rules.explanation: Scammers pose as a child or relative on a new number and then ask for urgent money. Call the person on their old number first.
patterns: \b(?:hi|hello|hey) (?:mum|mom|dad)\b[^.!?\n]{0,80}\b(?:new number|lost my phone|broke my phone|new phone)\b

rules.title: Asks you to install an app or remote-access tool
rules.explanation: Remote-access tools and unknown APK files give a scammer control of your phone or computer and your banking apps.

rules.title: Tells you to click a link
rules.explanation: Links in unexpected messages are the main way phishing works. Go to the official app or website yourself instead.
